label: merkle-sha256-cuda
note: SHA-256 CUDA Merkle over Candidate B Ligero shape (310602 rows x 16384 cols, 20.4 GB): full tree 446 GB/s, 0.36 M leaves/s, 45.6 ms/batch = 11.1 us/VU; A shape 425 GB/s. Chunked-leaf variant 624 GB/s. Replaces tensor.md's assumed 50 GB/s: B hash share drops 70% -> 9% (4090 measured) / 7% (H100 bandwidth scaling x3.32); B is a matmul problem, not a hashing problem, for SHA-256/Blake3 leaves. Overhead is tensor.py's model with one input replaced; bit-exact vs hashlib.

label: merkle-blake3-cuda
note: Blake3 CUDA Merkle (spec chunk tree, bit-exact vs blake3 PyPI) over B shape: full tree 359 GB/s, 56.7 ms/batch = 13.8 us/VU, B hash share 11%; A shape 347 GB/s. Generic 2^27 32-byte leaves: 87 GB/s, 2.7 G leaves/s.

label: merkle-poseidon2-babybear-cuda
note: Poseidon2/BabyBear width-16 fused CUDA kernel (Montgomery, Plonky3 constants, bit-exact vs Python ref matching Plonky3 vectors): 1.68 G perm/s; B shape full tree 57.7 GB/s = 86 us/VU, B hash share 44% on 4090; width-24: 34.2 GB/s, 146 us/VU. Torch elementwise int64 0.4 GB/s; torch INT8-limb tensor-core MDS (torch._int_mm) 0.3 GB/s -- slower than elementwise (limb split/recombine dominates; MDS-only 8.6 ms vs 4.4 ms per 2^20 states). Poseidon2 does NOT reach 200 GB/s; hashing remains B's bucket if leaves must be algebraic.
